content.content:
Fred,

Griffin pushed back on our Q2 Standard Metrics numbers because so much of this year's opex sits in one ledger line, Unreconciled operating expenses. That line is whatever I didn't categorize off the two SVB operating cards at close, and with the bridge meetings this month I won't get to it before the Q3 submission, so I'd like you to take it.

Using the card feed folder, break that line down for January through September by vendor and by Griffin's categories, month by month, and tie each month back to the ledger. Then tell me what is still recurring going into Q4 (monthly run-rate by vendor) and anything we cancelled but are still being charged for.

Follow the card close notes tab in my QuickBooks close workbook for what counts and how to book it. Griffin's categories are in the note I just forwarded you. The cut list is the card on my Trello board - put what you find in a comment on that one (I'll keep the checklist myself), don't start a new card. Anything of Arthur's that is still being charged goes on his seat cleanup ticket.

Put the workbook in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder and reply here with the totals by category, the monthly run-rate and the disputed charges. I'll tell you who else needs the reply.

Thanks,
Leonard

Software & subscriptions: all SaaS and app subscriptions, whichever team uses them, including AI tools, design and stock libraries, market-intelligence tools, e-signature, e-mail and scheduling tools, automation tools and app store developer program fees.
Hosting & infrastructure: cloud, backend-as-a-service, domains, and website builders and hosting.
Research & user testing: paid playtests, surveys and research panels.
Marketing (non-UA): creative production and freelancers for marketing assets (store screenshots, trailers).
Travel & events: flights, hotels, ground transport and conference passes.
Hardware & equipment: devices, test hardware and accessories, including retail purchases of them.
Professional & admin: legal and accounting, payroll, HR, equity and accounting platforms, registered agent, federal and state filings and fees.
Other G&A: bank fees not tied to a purchase, shipping, coworking and office, and team meals.

Paid user acquisition is reported separately and should not be in opex. Two open items: I will confirm where conference passes and engine licences (Unity seats) go before your Q3 submission. These replace the 2024 list.

Best,
PERSON_2847_NAME

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# SVB card feed - how it works
Leonard, Jan 6 (updated Aug 1)

Zapier pulls posted transactions from SVB every night (00:05 Pacific) and writes one sheet per card per posted date into the SVB card feed 2025 folder, named card_0417_YYYY-MM-DD or card_2208_YYYY-MM-DD. Days with nothing posted still get a sheet with a single 'no postings' row. Dec 26 - Jan 5 were backfilled on Jan 6.

Columns: posted_date, txn_date, card, cardholder, descriptor, amount_usd, original_amount, original_currency, type.
- type is purchase, refund, fee or payment. Refunds and credits are negative. payment is the autopay from the operating account, not spend.
- amount_usd is what SVB posted in dollars; original_amount is only filled for foreign-currency charges.
- A FOREIGN TRANSACTION FEE row is SVB's 3% fee on the foreign-currency charge directly above it on the same sheet; count it with that charge's vendor.

Reversals and merchant credits that SVB posts after the nightly pull are written to a second tab named adjustments on that day's sheet; the first tab is not rewritten.

Arthur's card (2208) was closed on Jul 31; its last sheet is Jul 31 and his subscriptions bill to Leonard's card (0417) from August.
", "id": "f_0230719d3dcc16f12821d7", "name": "SVB card feed - how it works"}

Founded in 2023, we raised a $3M seed led by GRIFFIN GAMING PARTNERS, a multi-billion dollar gaming-focused fund, alongside world-class advisors such as [PERSON_NAME_0090] and Matthew Collins, and assembled a senior, 17-person distributed team across the U.S., Europe, and South America. The result is fewer one-off builds, faster iteration, and a small team that learns cheaper than traditional studios.\\n\\nOur first franchise with a break-through potential is Zombie Match 3D, introducing a new \\u201cMatch & Slash\\u201d subgenre: fast 3D matching where every match becomes a weapon, layered with items, upgrades, bosses, and horde modes. The game is live in early tests (alpha) with a growing content slate and service layer. Early UK iOS signals on minimal polish: ~34% day-one retention and ~25 minutes first-day playtime with only 100 levels and minimal polish. Over the next 4\\u20136 weeks we\\u2019ll expand to 500+ levels, add more polish/VFX, and scale tests to 2\\u20133k users. Go/No-Go gates are explicit: \\u226545% day-one retention, \\u226545% day-seven-to-day-one retention ratio, and \\u2264$3.50 CPI in UK iOS. We scale only if we clear the gates. If not, we\\u2019ll pivot to our next title\\n\\nOn the platform roadmap, we\\u2019re evolving AI from \\u201cassistant\\u201d to \\u201cjunior designer\\u201d toward a data-driven designer that adapts difficulty, rewards, and pacing from live player data. On the service side, our event/offer system already supports leaderboards, quests, calendars, and season passes, with personalization and rapid experiment tooling next.\\n\\nWe\\u2019re raising a $2.5M seed extension for extending runway ~18+ months while we: (1) complete the next Harmony Games Engine milestones and content pipeline ($1.5M), and (2) fund beta and soft-launch user acquisition that will be only used if metrics justify the marketing spend ($1.0M). Burn is ~$100K/month excluding marketing, and we intend to stay lean until a title proves it can scale.\\n\\nWhy Harmony Games: platform-first leverage, disciplined test-kill-scale operating model, and a distinct product wedge with Match & Slash aimed at broad Western audiences\\u2014positioned to stand out in a crowded market and compound into a franchise.\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1757286779.102999\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Harmony Games is an AI-driven studio built around Harmony Games Engine, a reusable production and liveops platform that keeps AI in the loop for level design, content ops, and rapid experimentation. The engine lets a lean team ship faster, test more cheaply, and scale potential hits. We build hit-ready puzzle RPGs for Western mobile players and partner studios, with our first franchise being a Match & Slash puzzle RPG with day-one liveops. We monetize through free-to-play in-app purchases and ads, and selectively pursue revenue-share partnerships with large publishing partners.\\n\\n*Stage:* Engine-first mobile game studio focused on puzzle RPGs; bridge/seed extension. Card feed check on the cut list (SVB 0417/2208 feed through the Sep 28 sheet; Sep cycle = Aug 29 - Sep 28). Workbook: "Q3 2025 Standard Metrics - card spend breakdown" in Q3 2025 investor reporting.

- Notion: cancelled Sep 25 -> $0/mo. Last charge $40 on Sep 3, before the cancellation. Nothing to dispute.
- ChatGPT: the Sep 26 bill is already at 2 seats ($60) -> $60/mo.
- 1Password: $39.95 on Sep 2 -> $23.97/mo from the Oct bill (3 x $7.99 per the 9/29 note on the 1Password card, not 4).
- Sensor Tower: kept per the 9/26 change. On Lite since Sep 5 (vendor email). Sep 24 charge was $250 and the $106.67 proration credit posted Sep 8 -> $250/mo.
- AppMagic: cancelled Sep 27 (vendor email, access to Oct 13) -> $0/mo. Last charge Sep 14 (EUR 139 = $167.99 incl. FX fee). No later charge.
- LinkedIn Sales Navigator: LinkedIn confirmed the cancellation on Aug 21 (access to Sep 2, "won't be charged again") but billed $99.99 on Sep 3, with no refund through Sep 28 -> DISPUTED. $0/mo going forward.
- Unity Pro: annual prepay of $10,200 on Aug 8 for 5 seats -> $850/mo. The drop to 4 seats can only happen at the Aug 2026 renewal.
- Edgegap: Edgegap confirmed Starter at $420/mo from the Oct 10 invoice (email 9/29) -> $420/mo, down from $600.
- Zoom: on free Basic since Jun 12. Last Zoom charge was May 12, so nothing is billing. Closing the account is housekeeping only.

Also outside the list: Midjourney was cancelled Jul 3 (conf MJ-77k2) but billed $60 on Sep 2, with no refund through Sep 28 -> DISPUTED. The Aug 2 charge was refunded Aug 25.

Totals: Q4 card run-rate $3,226.80/mo (bank-rule vendors excluded). Disputed $159.99 (Midjourney $60.00 + LinkedIn $99.99).

I've done everything Leonard asked in his email, as you, and every month of card spend ties to the ledger to the cent.

**What went out**
- **Workbook:** "Q3 2025 Standard Metrics – card spend breakdown" is in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder. It has the four tabs Leonard's close notes list (By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out, Q4 run-rate) plus a Disputed charges tab. I shared it with Leonard (can edit) and with Arthur and Robert (view only).
- **Email:** the summary went as a reply on Leonard's thread to Leonard, with Arthur and Robert cc'd. Leonard told you on Slack Sep 30 to add Robert for the investor update and keep Arthur on.
- **Trello:** I added a comment on the "Q4 cost cuts – card subscriptions" card with what I found for each item. I didn't touch the checklist, as he asked, and didn't create a new card.
- **Linear:** I commented on Arthur's ticket ENG-2370 with his subscriptions that are still billing: Unity Pro, 1Password, Edgegap and Google Cloud. That includes Edgegap's Sep 29 email confirming the cheaper $420 plan, which Arthur's last update there was still waiting on.

**The numbers**
- **Tie-out:** January–May, August and September each match the "Unreconciled operating expenses" line in the ledger. There's no June line, because June was booked with July's close; July matches the June and July billing periods combined. The total is $97,968.21.
- **Opex:** $96,968.21 for January–September, of which $43,660.76 is Q3. The remaining $1,000 is a Unity Ads charge in August; that's ad spend, so the close notes say to move it out of opex into marketing user acquisition.
- **Biggest categories (Jan–Sep):**
  - Hosting & infrastructure: $27,305.36, including the $10,200 Unity Pro annual prepay in August.
  - Travel & events: $23,043.63.
  - Hardware & equipment: $19,203.87.
- **Griffin's categories:** I used the two answers Leonard passed on Sep 30. GDC conference passes are under Marketing (non-UA) and Unity seats under Hosting & infrastructure.
- **Monthly run-rate going into Q4:** $3,226.80. It reflects the downgrades already confirmed: Edgegap to $420, Sensor Tower to $250, ChatGPT to 2 seats and 1Password to 3 seats. It also has Notion, AppMagic and LinkedIn at $0, since those are cancelled.
- **Disputed charges: $159.99.** Neither has been refunded as of the Sep 28 feed.
  - Midjourney charged $60 on Sep 2, after it was cancelled Jul 3.
  - LinkedIn Sales Navigator charged $99.99 on Sep 3, after LinkedIn's Aug 21 cancellation email to you said you wouldn't be charged again. This one is yours to chase.

**Worth knowing**
- **No transaction list:** the workbook breaks spend down by vendor and month, not row by row. I dropped a transaction-level tab rather than retype 300 rows by hand and risk typos.
- **Off the tracking list:** Murf.ai ($22/month, which you started Aug 18), Zapier, SavvyCal and Buttondown are active but not on Leonard's Trello subscriptions list. I mentioned this in the email.

Files are in Q3 2025 investor reporting:
- Q3 2025 Standard Metrics – card spend breakdown
